prompt: Write an email to a colleague about the first week of planting a vegetable garden. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the email only.
final_message:
Subject: Week One in the Vegetable Garden

Hi Sam,

You asked me to let you know how the garden was going, so here's an update on the first week. It was busier than I expected, but I'm happy with how it went.

I started on Saturday by clearing the bed. The grass and weeds came up more easily than I feared, though I spent a solid two hours with a garden fork and a lot of stubborn roots. After that, I worked in about three inches of compost and turned it into the top eight inches of soil. I'd recommend not skipping this step. The difference in texture was obvious, going from heavy clay to something dark and crumbly.

On Sunday I did the planting. I put in lettuce, spinach, radishes, and carrots, since they handle cooler weather well. I also set out a few broccoli seedlings from the nursery. I spaced everything according to the seed packets, although I suspect I was a bit too cautious and could have squeezed in more. I labeled each row with a plant marker, which I'm glad I did, because the seedlings look remarkably alike at this stage.

Watering has been the main daily task. I've been giving the bed a gentle soak each morning, because the seeds need consistent moisture to germinate. On Wednesday we had an unexpected cold snap, so I covered the broccoli with a sheet overnight. It seemed fine the next day, which was a relief.

The first real sign of progress came on Thursday, when the radishes poked through. Radishes are famously fast, but it was still satisfying to see actual green after four days of staring at bare dirt. The lettuce followed on Friday, and I'm waiting on the carrots, which I know can take up to three weeks.

Not everything went perfectly. I noticed some slug damage on a couple of the broccoli leaves, so I'm going to try a shallow dish of beer as a trap this week. I'll let you know whether it works. I also realized I should have put a layer of mulch down sooner to help hold in moisture, so that's on my list for the weekend.

Overall, my biggest lesson is that preparation matters more than anything else. The time I spent on the soil seems to be paying off already.

If you're still thinking about starting your own bed, I'd be glad to share my seed list or come over and help you get set up. We could even swap seedlings later in the season.

How are your tomatoes doing, by the way?

Best,
[name]
